extraction.segment_function: The block analyzes the revelatory quality of speech and action in human togetherness, contrasting it with anonymity (good works and crime), discussing how action loses its unique character when reduced to means-ends achievement, and examining the intangibility and philosophic difficulty of expressing the unique 'who' of a person in language.

claims.claim: The revelatory quality of speech and action emerges in sheer human togetherness where people are neither for nor against each other.
claims.supporting_excerpt: This revelatory quality of speech and action comes to the fore where people are with others and neither for nor against them—that is, in sheer human togetherness.

claims.claim: When action loses the disclosure of the agent and becomes merely a means to an end, it ceases to transcend productive activity.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Without the disclosure of the agent in the act, action loses its specific character and becomes one form of achievement among others.

must_not_be_lost: Action needs the public realm and glory to fully disclose the agent together with the act.
Attempts to state who somebody is in words tend to describe what he is as a type or character, missing his specific uniqueness.
